summary.headline: Cosmic CRF H2 FY26 revenue rose 77% YoY to INR412 crore, but FY26 PAT margin slipped to ~7% and Amzen LOI is still pending CoC approval.
summary.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 consolidated revenue up 77% YoY to INR412 crore from INR232 crore, with EBITDA up 81% and net profit up 128%. Full-year consolidated revenue rose about 78% to roughly INR722 crore, EBITDA about 77% and PAT about 74%, though management conceded PAT margin was about 7% versus a restated ~6% base. Installed capacity reached 133,600 MT with actual production of about 106,370 MT, and the order book stands at INR760 crore. The H1 bidder status for Amzen Transportation was described as reinstated after Supreme Court rulings, with the CoC approval and LOI still awaited.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR90 crore negative in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Working capital debt (SBI and Bank of India)

financial_highlights.value: INR67 crore with about INR1.5 crore profit

segments.name: Cosmic CRF standalone
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 55,000 MT per annum; four plants on 14 acres covering about 75% of wagon and coach body manufacturing. Capacity added via two new sheds (6,000 and 11,000 sq ft) and cutting and slitting lines, with capex of over INR30 crore in the year.

segments.name: NS Engineering Projects (NSEPL, 74% owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 65,000 MT, up from about 12,500 MT when acquired. Produced 56,380 MT in FY26; galvanizing bath running at about 24,000 MT per year, with a plan to scale to about 85,000 MT in the same space.

segments.name: Cosmic Springs and Engineers (CSEL, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 13,600 MT, produced about 7,300 MT per management. Springs output about 2,300 MT at near-zero margin pending RDSO licence; forging unit targeted for commercial production within about nine months.

segments.name: Amzen Transportation (pending acquisition)
segments.commentary: Wagon capacity 3,600 per annum, targeted to rise to 7,200 with capex; also bridge girders up to 20,000 MT per RDSO approval. Management estimates the total project cost at about INR400-odd crore and plans sea freight containers at about 7,500 to 10,000 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance: installed capacity of roughly 122,000 to 130,000 MT, with output at 88-89% utilisation; management said the company should reach about 175,000 MT in 12-15 months.
Management said FY27 top line should be at least about 30% higher than FY26, with a 20-25% upside if the infrastructure and railway cycle holds.
Target of about 350,000 MT by FY29 across all units including Amzen; at about INR100,000 per tonne, management indicated about INR3,500 crore revenue.
Springs margin expected to rise to about 10% and then 15-18% PAT after RDSO licence, which management expects by next month.

Amzen timeline: LOI by June, then 90 days of approvals and repairs, with first commercial production targeted within about nine to twelve months; expected Amzen capex of about INR200 crore funded by debt.
Management said the company will apply for main board migration in early July 2026 once eligibility is met, and said raw material prices could rise 7-10% in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 133,600 MT as of date; actual production about 106,370 MT in FY26 versus 55,000-56,000 MT last year.
Forging unit under construction, with commercial production targeted in about nine months.
NSEPL galvanizing expansion on newly acquired adjacent land, adding about 20,000 MT of installed capacity.
RDSO licence for springs is pending after about 75% of testing is done; management expects approval next month.
Amzen capex to lift wagon capacity from 3,600 to 7,200 per annum over about two years.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR760 crore covering infra and railway items, up from INR500-550 crore last year.
Management expects raw material prices to rise 7-10% in H2 FY27, with long-term contracts and price variation clauses used to pass through costs.
Raw material pricing moved from about INR52,000-53,000 per tonne last year to about INR60,000 this year, per management.
Management cited a possible railway procurement of 1 lakh wagons (about INR40,000 crore TAM) and an industry capacity of about 40,000-45,000 wagons per year.
West Bengal government infrastructure expansion (metro, bridges, cofferdams, sheet piles, crash barriers) cited as a potential order source; no specific orders named.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and volumes for springs and forgings in FY26, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Springs volume about 2,300 MT and total fabrication plus steel about 4,500 MT. Springs revenue INR67 crore but profit only about INR1.5 crore because RDSO licence is pending and sales go to traders, not railways. Forging has not started.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin dilute in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three reasons: weak springs profitability, about INR2-2.5 crore carrying cost of Amzen KMPs, and about INR10 crore legal and related costs on Amzen, which auditors did not allow to be capitalised. Total hit about INR8 crore to PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Amzen award final, and could anyone bid again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Supreme Court set aside the NCLAT order, restoring the H1 bidder status it held when the NCLAT order came; the CoC must now scrap the new Form G and resolution plans and negotiate with the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and funding plan for Amzen?
qa_highlights.answer: Term loan about INR36 crore plus working capital of INR84 crore from SBI and Bank of India; cash of about INR150 crore. Amzen is expected to need about INR200 crore of debt, with peak debt of about INR300 crore term and INR300 crore working capital by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from LOI to Amzen production?
qa_highlights.answer: LOI expected by June, then 60-90 days of repairs and AMCs, with first commercial production targeted by March-May 2027 and at most about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is 100% growth guidance still intact for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth of no less than 100% is the promoter's aspiration but could not be assured because raw material prices and government spending are outside its control; it framed FY27 at 30% or more.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material price volatility be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock levels, price variation clauses on railway contracts, traders for smaller purchases, and future hedging once volumes reach about 200,000 MT, plus liquid metal initiative for diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Would the NSEPL 26% minority buyout be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it wants to consolidate the 26% minority holding in NSEPL via a SEBI-route process, with a merchant banker report and shareholder approval, and said it is for consolidation only.

risks_watch: Amzen LOI and CoC approval are still pending; timing depends on procedural steps and possible further legal challenge, and the company's legal costs have already weighed on FY26 profit.
Springs business has near-zero margin until the RDSO licence is granted; a delay would continue to weigh on consolidated margins.
Raw material price volatility (steel, wheel sets) with management guiding for a 7-10% increase in H2 FY27 and limited contract pass-through on existing orders.
Cash conversion: operating cash flow only INR3.5 crore in FY26, with trade receivables and payables large and sensitive to government payment timing.
Interest cost of INR12.2 crore in FY26 and the planned debt build-up to roughly INR600 crore combined by FY29.
Main board migration application expected early July 2026 with a small eligibility gap still to be closed.
Dependence on railway and infrastructure budgets; the company acknowledged a slowdown in the railway tailwind over the last 1-1.5 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Amzen, growth and vision, with long narrative answers and repeated references to God and the promoter's personal vision. Notably more cautious on FY27 numbers, declining to give a specific figure and citing raw material and government-spending uncertainty.
key_quotes: The total order book that we are carrying right now is INR760 crores which is divided into two parts, the infrastructure items as well as the railway items.

So we will be able to do 175,000 metric tonnes in totality with NS Engineering, in totality in terms of volume with NS Engineering, with Cosmic CRF, with Cosmic Springs and Engineers forging division and Spring division.

I cannot control the market at large. So tomorrow, if railway decides to actually bring in 45,000 50,000 wagons at one go and there's a business, then believe me, you're not talking -- 100% is very less.

adds.what: NSEPL galvanizing expansion on adjacent land, adding ~20,000 MT installed capacity (scale to ~85,000 MT in same space)
CSEL forging unit (commercial production targeted ~9 months)
Amzen wagon capacity 3,600 to 7,200 per annum (capex over ~2 years), pending acquisition
Amzen bridge girders up to 20,000 MT per RDSO approval, pending acquisition

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top line at least 30% above FY26 (20-25% upside) and no less than 100% growth ex-Amzen over 1.5-2 years, backed by order book of INR760 crore (up from INR500-550 crore) and capacity rising to 122-130k MT in FY27 and ~175k MT in 12-15 months, though Amzen LOI/CoC approval is still pending and the 350k MT FY29 target lacks detailed capex.
